For dot-product logits zᵢ=hᵀeᵢ, direct algebra gives ∇ₕL=Σᵢ(∂L/∂zᵢ)eᵢ. Reciprocal rescaling h′=ch, e′ᵢ=eᵢ/c preserves logits and loss but divides the detached-feature gradient norm by |c|. Thus its magnitude is coordinate-dependent. This is a scoring-level identity; tied input/output embeddings mean that rescaling embeddings alone need not preserve the encoder’s outputs. Positive/negative BCE gives gₕ=(σ(z₊)−1)e₊+σ(z₋)e₋: substantial opposing contributions can cancel despite substantial logit derivatives. Measure each contribution, their cosine similarity, and ‖g₊+g₋‖/(‖g₊‖+‖g₋‖). Related research documents negatively correlated sample gradients as [gradient confusion](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/sankararaman20a.html).

Detaching h omits the encoder pathway. By the chain rule, backbone gradients are Jₕ,θᵀgₕ; Jacobian amplification, contraction and alignment determine their magnitude. Tied embeddings additionally receive both lookup/encoder and output-scoring contributions, which can reinforce or cancel. [Weight-tying analysis](https://aclanthology.org/E17-2025/) and [autograd documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/autograd.html) support examining these pathways separately and together.

Useful controls: log unreduced logit derivatives, margins and saturation; per-example feature-gradient norms versus the norm after averaging; feature/embedding norms; and full-backward parameter gradients by layer, before clipping and after mixed-precision unscaling. Keep examples, negative sampling, loss reduction and precision fixed. Measure actual optimizer steps ‖Δθ‖ and relative steps ‖Δθ‖/(‖θ‖+ε), plus resulting logit/loss changes. Adam’s moments, normalization, ε and weight decay make raw gradients insufficient proxies for updates; see the [Adam algorithm](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.optim.Adam.html) and [effective-step analysis](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2006.08217). These controls distinguish saturation, cancellation, parameter scale and encoder sensitivity.
